title: Participles 2: Active Past (-вший / -ший)
description: The active past participle: the noun performed the action at some prior time. Today: formation from the past-tense stem; both aspects form this participle; irregular consonant-stem variants take -ший instead of -вший.
descriptionRussian: Действительное причастие прошедшего времени: определяемое слово совершило действие в прошлом. Сегодня: образование от основы прошедшего времени; обе видовые формы образуют это причастие; основы на согласный получают суффикс -ший вместо -вший.
intro: The same idea shifted backwards in time, and this one has a wider reach: both aspects can form it, where the present-tense version was limited to imperfective verbs. That is because a past participle only needs a past stem, and every verb has one. Two suffixes cover it, chosen by whether the masculine past ends in a vowel or a consonant.
rules: An active past participle is a verb-derived adjective expressing an action the noun performed at some prior moment: the man who had read → прочитавший мужчина.
Formation: from the past-tense stem (drop -л from the masculine past), add -вш + adjective endings (-ий, -ая, -ее, -ие). Читал → читавший; прочитал → прочитавший.
Verbs whose masculine past ends in a consonant (нёс, мог, вёл, шёл) add -ш + endings instead of -вш: нёсший, могший, ведший, шедший. The шедший form for идти uses the irregular past-stem шед-.
BOTH imperfective and perfective verbs form active past participles. Imperfective expresses ongoing past activity; perfective expresses completed prior action.
examples: Прочитавший статью студент закрыл журнал. (The student who had read the article closed the magazine.)

items.prompt: Recap from L1: what is the active present participle of читать?
items.promptEnglish: Form the active present participle of читать.
items.hint: Recap: from читают, drop the personal ending and add -ющ- + adjective ending.
items.explanation: Recap from L1: читают → чита- + -ющ- + -ий = читающий (active PRESENT participle). Today's lesson covers the active PAST form (читавший), formed from the past-tense stem instead. Читая is the imperfective verbal adverb (verbal-adverbs track); читать is the infinitive.

items.prompt: What is the active past participle of прочитать?
items.promptEnglish: Form the active past participle of прочитать.
items.hint: From прочитал, drop -л and add -вш- + adjective ending.
items.explanation: Прочитал → прочита- + -вш- + -ий = прочитавший (the one who had read). Прочитав is the perfective verbal adverb; прочитанный is the passive past participle (lesson 4); прочитающий is not a real word (perfective verbs have no present-tense base, so they form no active present participle).

items.prompt: What is the active past participle of нести (past: нёс, несла)?
items.promptEnglish: Form the active past participle of нести.
items.hint: The past-tense masculine form нёс ends in a consonant. Which suffix follows that pattern?
items.explanation: Нёс ends in a consonant (the -л was dropped historically), so the active past participle takes -ш-, not -вш-: нёс- + -ш- + -ий = нёсший. The -вш- pattern requires a vowel-final stem; consonant-final stems (нёс, мог, шёл, вёл) take the shorter -ш-. Нёсая and Нёсши are not real Russian forms.

items.prompt: What is the active past participle of reflexive вернуться?
items.promptEnglish: Form the active past participle of вернуться.
items.hint: Reflexive verbs add -вшийся (instead of -вший) to keep the reflexive marker.
items.explanation: Вернуться is reflexive (ends in -ться). The active past participle is formed from the past stem верну- with -вшийся: вернувшийся (the one who returned). Вернувшись is the perfective verbal adverb (verbal-adverbs track); возвращавшийся is the active past participle of imperfective возвращаться (the aspect partner); возвращающийся is the active present of возвращаться.

items.prompt: Прочитавший статью студент закрыл журнал. What does прочитавший mean?
items.promptEnglish: Translate прочитавший in the sentence above.
items.hint: Прочитавший is the active past participle of perfective прочитать.
items.explanation: Прочитавший is the active past participle of perfective прочитать. The perfective aspect signals that the reading was completed before the main verb (закрыл). The English 'who had read' captures the prior-completion reading. The imperfective active past form (читавший) would mean 'who had been reading' (ongoing past activity).

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Active past participle (perfective): the student finished reading before asking. Modifies студент as an adjective.
hints: The reading is finished before the question is asked. Which active participle form expresses prior completion?
explanations: Прочитавший is the active past participle of perfective прочитать. The reading was completed before the question was asked. Читающий is the active PRESENT participle (would mean 'who is currently reading,' simultaneous reading); прочитав is the perfective verbal adverb (a different form, verbal-adverbs track); прочитанный is the PASSIVE past participle (lesson 4) and would describe the article, not the student.

errorCorrection.sentence: Вёзвший продукты водитель остановился у магазина.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The driver who was transporting the groceries stopped by the shop.
errorCorrection.explanation: When the masculine past ends in a consonant (вёз, no -л), the active past suffix is bare -ш, not -вш: вёзший. The -вш variant attaches only to vowel-final past stems (читал → читавший); a consonant stem takes plain -ш.

errorCorrection.sentence: Пришёлший на встречу гость снял пальто.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The guest who had arrived at the meeting took off his coat.
errorCorrection.explanation: Прийти forms its active past from the irregular stem -шед-, plus -ш: пришедший. Building the participle straight off the masculine past пришёл produces пришёлший, but the -л drops and the stem vowel changes, exactly as in шёл → шедший.

errorCorrection.sentence: Одевший тепло ребёнок вышел во двор.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The warmly dressed child went out into the yard.
errorCorrection.explanation: Одеться is reflexive, so its active past participle keeps the -ся: одевшийся. Dropping the -ся gives одевший, which belongs to the transitive одеть 'to dress (someone else)' and would need an object. Одевшись is the gerund, not a participle.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each verb by which past-participle suffix it takes.

reviewVocab.definition: active past participle (the noun performed the action at some prior moment; both aspects form this participle)
reviewVocab.example: Читавший, прочитавший, сказавший, нёсший, шедший — все это действительные причастия прошедшего времени.

reviewVocab.definition: past-tense stem (drop -л from the masculine past form to get it; consonant-stem verbs use the masculine past form as-is)
reviewVocab.example: Читал → чита- (основа прошедшего времени) + вш + ий = читавший.

reviewVocab.definition: consonant (verbs whose masculine past form ends in a consonant - нёс, мог, вёл, шёл: take -ш- instead of -вш-)
reviewVocab.example: Нёс оканчивается на согласный, поэтому: нёс + ш + ий = нёсший.

reviewVocab.definition: reflexive verb (ends in -ться; its active past participle keeps the reflexive marker as -вшийся)
